Name: Shell_75mm
---: French Soixante-Quinze - most common shell at Verdun (~65% of French fire)
HistoricalNote: The 75mm was the primary French field gun. Its flat trajectory gave soldiers as little as 1-2 seconds warning.

Name: Shell_77mm
---: German Feldkanone 96 n.A. - German equivalent of the French 75
HistoricalNote: German soldiers called the sound 'whizz-bang' — it arrived almost simultaneously with the sound of firing.

Name: Shell_155mm
---: 155mm C/1915 Howitzer - medium artillery, high arc trajectory
HistoricalNote: High-angle howitzers gave soldiers 6-10 seconds warning — enough time to flatten yourself if you heard it in time.

Name: Shell_210mm
HistoricalNote: The 210mm made a distinctive freight-train rumble. Soldiers had 10-15 seconds warning — but surviving a direct hit was virtually impossible.

Name: Shell_305mm
---: 305mm Siege Mortar - rare but psychologically devastating
HistoricalNote: Known as 'gros Bertha' class. The 20+ second incoming sound was uniquely terrifying. Craters 5-8m wide, 3-4m deep.
